\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{મરણ} (maraṇ)}{મરણ (maraṇ)}]{\gu{મરણ} (maraṇ) — a death}

\label{lesson:GU-C499-maran}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a dowry, then the Gujarati for a divorce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{મરણ}}
\textbf{\gu{મરણ}} — \emph{maraṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}a death\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{દાદાના} \gu{મરણથી} \gu{આખા} \gu{કુટુંબને} \gu{દુઃખ} \gu{થયું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādānā maraṇthī ākhā kuṭumbne duḥkh thayũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The whole family grieved at my grandfather's death.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{મરણ}} (\emph{maraṇ}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{maraṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}dying\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists the Gujarati word (CDIAL 9869).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maraṇ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maraṇ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādānā maraṇthī ākhā kuṭumbne duḥkh thayũ.} — The whole family grieved at my grandfather's death.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a dowry, then the Gujarati for a divorce, then say \emph{maraṇ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{મરણ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A death\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અવસાન} (avsān)}{અવસાન (avsān)}]{\gu{અવસાન} (avsān) — a passing away}

\label{lesson:GU-C499-avsan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a divorce, then the Gujarati for a death.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અવસાન}}
\textbf{\gu{અવસાન}} — \emph{avsān} — \textquotedblleft{}a passing away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ગયા} \gu{મહિને} \gu{મારા} \gu{મામાનું} \gu{અવસાન} \gu{થયું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gayā mahine mārā māmānũ avsān thayũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle passed away last month.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અવસાન}} (\emph{avsān}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{avasāna}, which Monier-Williams lists under \emph{ava-so} as \textquotedblleft{}conclusion, termination\textquotedblright{} and also as \textquotedblleft{}death\textquotedblright{}; Gujarati uses it as the polite word for a death.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avsān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avsān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gayā mahine mārā māmānũ avsān thayũ.} — My uncle passed away last month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a divorce, then the Gujarati for a death, then say \emph{avsān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{અવસાન} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A passing away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગુજરવું} (gujarvũ)}{ગુજરવું (gujarvũ)}]{\gu{ગુજરવું} (gujarvũ) — to pass away}

\label{lesson:GU-C499-gujarvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a death, then the Gujarati for a passing away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગુજરવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ગુજરવું}} — \emph{gujarvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{દાદી} \gu{ઊંઘમાં} \gu{જ} \gu{ગુજરી} \gu{ગયાં}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī ū̃ghmā̃ ja gujrī gayā̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother passed away in her sleep.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \gu{તે} \gu{ગુજરી} \gu{ગયો}, \emph{te gujrī gayo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગુજરવું}} (\emph{gujarvũ}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{guzar-}, the stem of the verb \textquotedblleft{}to pass, go by\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gujarvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gujarvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādī ū̃ghmā̃ ja gujrī gayā̃.} — Grandmother passed away in her sleep.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a death, then the Gujarati for a passing away, then say \emph{gujarvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ગુજરવું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To pass away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બેસણું} (besṇũ)}{બેસણું (besṇũ)}]{\gu{બેસણું} (besṇũ) — a prayer meeting after a death}

\label{lesson:GU-C499-besnu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a passing away, then the Gujarati for to pass away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બેસણું}}
\textbf{\gu{બેસણું}} — \emph{besṇũ} — \textquotedblleft{}a prayer meeting after a death\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{સોમવારે} \gu{સાંજે} \gu{દાદાનું} \gu{બેસણું} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{somvāre sā̃je dādānũ besṇũ che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather's prayer meeting is on Monday evening.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બેસણું}} (\emph{besṇũ}) is built on \textbf{\gu{બેસવું}} (\emph{besvũ}), \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{}, which goes back to Sanskrit \emph{upaviśati}, \textquotedblleft{}sits down\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2245): the family sits together to receive visitors.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{besṇũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{besṇũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{somvāre sā̃je dādānũ besṇũ che.} — Grandfather's prayer meeting is on Monday evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a passing away, then the Gujarati for to pass away, then say \emph{besṇũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{બેસણું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A prayer meeting after a death\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અર્પવું} (arpavũ)}{અર્પવું (arpavũ)}]{\gu{અર્પવું} (arpavũ) — to offer with respect}

\label{lesson:GU-C499-arpavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to pass away, then the Gujarati for a prayer meeting after a death.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અર્પવું}}
\textbf{\gu{અર્પવું}} — \emph{arpavũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to offer with respect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બેસણામાં} \gu{બધાએ} \gu{દાદાના} \gu{ફોટાને} \gu{ફૂલ} \gu{અર્પ્યાં}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{besṇāmā̃ badhāe dādānā phoṭāne phūl arpyā̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the prayer meeting everyone offered flowers before my grandfather's photo.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{ફૂલ} \gu{અર્પ્યું}, \emph{teṇe phūl arpyũ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અર્પવું}} (\emph{arpavũ}) goes back to Sanskrit \emph{arpayati}, \textquotedblleft{}places upon, offers\textquotedblright{}, the causative of \emph{ṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}to go\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arpavũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{arpavũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{besṇāmā̃ badhāe dādānā phoṭāne phūl arpyā̃.} — At the prayer meeting everyone offered flowers before my grandfather's photo.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to pass away, then the Gujarati for a prayer meeting after a death, then say \emph{arpavũ} again
\end{itemize}
